column3: Valleys is plural, rather than singular “valley.”
The tree is rendered as an apple tree, rather than “apricot”; palate is rendered more generally as “taste.”
Raisin-cakes are named, rather than raisins alone.
The oath connects the animals with or, rather than “and.” The love itself chooses, rather than the impersonal “time is right.”
The opening is the noun voice or sound, rather than the command “Listen!”
The introductory verbs are answered and said; “with me” is not expressed.
The turtledove is singular, rather than plural “turtledoves.”
“With me” is not expressed in the invitation.
“His flock” supplies the unstated object of pasturing.
The day breathes in the Hebrew image, rather than explicitly breaking.
